title: PMBOK Framework Mastery Quiz
subtitle: Comprehensive assessment of the 5 Process Groups and 10 Knowledge Areas

questions.question: Which Process Group officially authorizes a project and produces the Project Charter?
questions.explanation: The Initiating Process Group is where the Project Charter is developed, officially authorizing the project and assigning the Project Manager.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area is responsible for creating the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)?
questions.explanation: Project Scope Management includes the process of creating the WBS, which decomposes the total project scope into manageable work packages.

questions.question: Which Process Group runs concurrently with the Executing Process Group throughout the project?
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Controlling runs parallel to Executing throughout the project lifecycle, continuously tracking performance and managing changes.

questions.question: Earned Value Management (EVM) is a key tool in which Knowledge Area?
questions.explanation: EVM is a core technique in Project Cost Management, used to measure project performance and forecast final costs (EAC, ETC).

questions.question: A project manager discovers that a key vendor may not deliver on time. Which Knowledge Area should have anticipated and planned for this?
questions.explanation: Project Risk Management should have identified vendor delivery delay as a risk, assessed its probability and impact, and prepared a contingency response plan.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area is the ONLY one present in all five Process Groups?
questions.explanation: Project Integration Management is the only Knowledge Area with processes in all five Process Groups, from Develop Project Charter (Initiating) to Close Project (Closing).

questions.question: The Lessons Learned Register is a key output of which Process Group?
questions.explanation: The Closing Process Group is where the PM formally documents lessons learned, archives project records, and obtains final acceptance from stakeholders.

questions.question: How many processes are contained in the Planning Process Group according to PMBOK 6th Edition?
questions.explanation: The Planning Process Group contains 24 processes, making it the most process-rich group in PMBOK and the blueprint for all subsequent execution.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key activity in the Initiating Process Group?
questions.explanation: Creating the Work Breakdown Structure is a Planning activity, not an Initiating activity. Initiating focuses on authorization and stakeholder identification.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Project Management Plan?
options: To serve as the blueprint for execution and control
questions.explanation: The Project Management Plan, developed in Planning, serves as the comprehensive blueprint for how the project will be executed, monitored, and controlled.

questions.question: Which Process Group contains only 1 process according to PMBOK 6th Edition?
questions.explanation: The Closing Process Group contains only 1 process: Close Project or Phase, which formally completes the project and archives all documentation.

questions.question: Scope creep is primarily prevented through which Knowledge Area?
questions.explanation: Project Scope Management ensures clear scope boundaries and prevents unauthorized additions that would blow up budget and schedule.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary deliverable of the Planning Process Group?
questions.explanation: While the Project Charter is actually produced in Initiating, the Planning group produces the Project Management Plan, WBS, Schedule Baseline, and Cost Baseline as key deliverables.

questions.question: The Critical Path Method (CPM) is primarily used in which Knowledge Area?
questions.explanation: CPM is a core technique in Project Schedule Management used to identify the longest sequence of dependent activities and protect them from delays.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area focuses on ensuring the project satisfies the needs for which it was undertaken?
questions.explanation: Project Quality Management ensures that deliverables meet defined standards and satisfy stakeholder requirements through planning, assurance, and control.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of the Executing Process Group?
questions.explanation: The Executing Process Group carries out the work defined in the project management plan, where the majority of the budget is consumed and actual deliverables are produced.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a process in Project Resource Management?
questions.explanation: Validate Scope is a Scope Management process. Resource Management processes include Estimate Activity Resources, Acquire Resources, Develop Team, Manage Team, and Control Resources.

questions.question: How many Knowledge Areas are defined in the PMBOK framework?
questions.explanation: The PMBOK framework defines 10 Knowledge Areas that represent specialized domains of project management expertise.

questions.question: A RACI matrix is primarily used in which Knowledge Area?
questions.explanation: A RACI matrix (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) is a key tool in Project Resource Management for clarifying roles and responsibilities.

questions.question: Which Process Group is responsible for integrated change control?
questions.explanation: Integrated Change Control is performed in the Monitoring and Controlling Process Group to evaluate and approve or reject all change requests across the project.

questions.question: What does EAC stand for in the context of Earned Value Management?
questions.explanation: EAC (Estimate At Completion) is a forecast of the total project cost at completion based on current performance trends.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between Executing and Monitoring & Controlling?
options: Parallel — M&C runs concurrently with Executing
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Controlling runs parallel to Executing throughout the project lifecycle, continuously tracking performance and initiating corrective actions.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area is responsible for managing the project's budget?
questions.explanation: Project Cost Management involves planning, estimating, budgeting, and controlling costs to ensure the project stays within the approved budget.

questions.question: What is the primary output of the Initiating Process Group?
questions.explanation: The Project Charter is the primary output of Initiating, officially authorizing the project and assigning the Project Manager.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area deals with identifying, analyzing, and responding to project risks?
questions.explanation: Project Risk Management includes processes to identify, analyze, and respond to both threats and opportunities to maximize project success probability.

questions.question: How many total processes are contained in all five Process Groups according to PMBOK 6th Edition?
questions.explanation: PMBOK 6th Edition contains 49 total processes distributed across the five Process Groups: 2 in Initiating, 24 in Planning, 10 in Executing, 12 in M&C, and 1 in Closing.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area is responsible for identifying and engaging stakeholders?
questions.explanation: Project Stakeholder Management includes processes to identify people, groups, or organizations that could impact or be impacted by the project and develop engagement strategies.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Stakeholder Register?
options: To document all identified stakeholders and their characteristics
questions.explanation: The Stakeholder Register, produced in Initiating, documents all identified stakeholders, their interests, influence, and engagement strategies.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area is responsible for managing vendor contracts and external procurement?
questions.explanation: Project Procurement Management manages the processes of purchasing or acquiring products, services, or results needed from outside the project team.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of Project Communications Management?
options: Ensuring timely and appropriate information distribution
questions.explanation: Project Communications Management ensures timely and appropriate planning, collection, creation, distribution, storage, and management of project information.

questions.question: Which Process Group produces the Schedule Baseline?
questions.explanation: The Schedule Baseline is produced in the Planning Process Group as part of the Project Management Plan and serves as the approved schedule for the project.

questions.question: What does CPI stand for in Earned Value Management?
questions.explanation: CPI (Cost Performance Index) measures the efficiency of cost spending. A CPI of 0.85 means $1 spent yields only $0.85 of value.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of the Planning Process Group?
options: It is the shortest process group
questions.explanation: The Planning Process Group contains 24 processes, making it the most process-rich group and the blueprint for all subsequent execution and control.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area includes the process of collecting and defining project requirements?
questions.explanation: Project Scope Management includes the Collect Requirements process, which gathers and documents stakeholder needs and expectations.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Executing Process Group?
options: To produce actual project deliverables and work products
questions.explanation: The Executing Process Group carries out the work defined in the project management plan, producing actual deliverables and consuming the majority of project resources.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a process in Project Schedule Management?
questions.explanation: Validate Scope is a Scope Management process. Schedule Management processes include Define Activities, Sequence Activities, Estimate Durations, Develop Schedule, and Control Schedule.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of Quality Control in Project Quality Management?
questions.explanation: Quality Control focuses on monitoring and controlling project deliverables to ensure they meet defined quality standards and acceptance criteria.

questions.question: Which Process Group is responsible for obtaining formal acceptance of deliverables?
questions.explanation: The Closing Process Group is responsible for obtaining final acceptance of deliverables from stakeholders and formally completing the project.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area focuses on ensuring the project team has the skills and resources needed?
questions.explanation: Project Resource Management includes processes to acquire, develop, and manage the project team to ensure they have the necessary skills and resources.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Cost Baseline?
options: To serve as the approved budget for measuring performance
questions.explanation: The Cost Baseline, produced in Planning, serves as the approved budget against which project spending is measured and performance is evaluated.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of Monitoring and Controlling?
options: To track, review, and regulate project progress and performance
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Controlling tracks, reviews, and regulates project progress and performance, identifying deviations and initiating corrective or preventive actions.

questions.question: What is the primary output of the Closing Process Group?
questions.explanation: The Closing Process Group produces the Lessons Learned Register, Final Project Report, Closed Contracts, and formal acceptance sign-off.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area includes the process of identifying and analyzing project risks?
questions.explanation: Project Risk Management includes processes to identify risks, perform qualitative and quantitative analysis, plan responses, and monitor risks throughout the project.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)?
options: To decompose project scope into manageable work packages
questions.explanation: The WBS decomposes the total project scope into manageable work packages, providing the foundation for planning, scheduling, and cost estimation.

questions.question: Which Process Group contains 12 processes according to PMBOK 6th Edition?
questions.explanation: The Monitoring and Controlling Process Group contains 12 processes focused on tracking, reviewing, and regulating project performance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key activity in the Executing Process Group?
questions.explanation: Creating the Work Breakdown Structure is a Planning activity. Executing activities include directing work, acquiring team members, managing communications, and conducting procurements.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of Project Integration Management?
options: Coordinating all project processes into a cohesive whole
questions.explanation: Project Integration Management coordinates all project management processes and activities into a cohesive whole, ensuring decisions in one area are reflected across all areas.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area is responsible for ensuring scope changes are properly evaluated and approved?
questions.explanation: Project Integration Management includes Integrated Change Control, which evaluates and approves or rejects all change requests, including scope changes.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Stakeholder Engagement Plan?
options: To define how stakeholders will be engaged and communicated with
questions.explanation: The Stakeholder Engagement Plan, produced in Planning, defines strategies for engaging stakeholders based on their power, interest, and influence.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary deliverable of the Executing Process Group?
questions.explanation: The Executing Process Group produces actual work products and deliverables, along with issue logs, change requests, and team performance assessments.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of the Initiating Process Group?
options: To define and authorize the project
questions.explanation: The Initiating Process Group defines and authorizes the project or a new phase, capturing the vision and identifying stakeholders.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area includes the process of controlling project scope?
questions.explanation: Project Scope Management includes the Control Scope process, which monitors and controls changes to the project scope.

questions.question: What does SPI stand for in Earned Value Management?
questions.explanation: SPI (Schedule Performance Index) measures the efficiency of schedule performance. An SPI of 0.9 means the project is 90% efficient in terms of schedule.

questions.question: Which Process Group is responsible for archiving project documents and releasing resources?
questions.explanation: The Closing Process Group is responsible for archiving project documents, releasing project resources, and formally completing the project.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between Scope, Schedule, and Cost in project management?
options: They are independent of each other
Changes in one typically impact the others
Only Scope affects Schedule and Cost
Only Cost affects Scope and Schedule
questions.explanation: Scope, Schedule, and Cost are interconnected. A scope change typically impacts the schedule and budget, which is why integrated change control is essential.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Risk Register?
options: To document identified risks, their analysis, and response plans
questions.explanation: The Risk Register, produced in Planning, documents all identified risks, their probability and impact, and planned responses.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area is responsible for managing project team performance?
questions.explanation: Project Resource Management includes the Manage Team process, which tracks team performance, resolves conflicts, and manages team development.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of the Develop Project Management Plan process?
options: To create the comprehensive plan for executing and controlling the project
questions.explanation: The Develop Project Management Plan process, part of Planning, creates the comprehensive plan that integrates all subsidiary plans and serves as the blueprint for execution.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of the Monitoring and Controlling Process Group?
options: It occurs only at the end of the project
It runs parallel to Executing throughout the project
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Controlling runs parallel to Executing throughout the project lifecycle, continuously tracking performance and managing changes.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Variance Analysis in project management?
options: To compare planned performance against actual performance and identify deviations
questions.explanation: Variance Analysis compares planned performance (baselines) against actual performance to identify deviations and trigger corrective actions.

questions.question: Which Knowledge Area includes the process of planning procurement strategies?
questions.explanation: Project Procurement Management includes the Plan Procurement Management process, which defines procurement strategies and approaches.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of the Direct and Manage Project Work process?
options: To perform the actual project work and produce deliverables
questions.explanation: Direct and Manage Project Work is the primary process in Executing where the actual project work is performed and deliverables are produced.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Knowledge Area in PMBOK?
questions.explanation: The correct Knowledge Area is Project Resource Management, not Project Team Management. Project Team Management is a process within Resource Management.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Perform Integrated Change Control process?
options: To evaluate, approve, or reject all change requests across the project
questions.explanation: Perform Integrated Change Control evaluates all change requests and ensures decisions in one area are reflected across schedule, cost, scope, and other areas.
